CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee injury

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient sustained a right knee injury one week ago while jumping on a trampoline at a trampoline park with his wife. This was his first time at a trampoline park. He heard a snap and experienced immediate pain. He heard a pop when he landed. He elevated the leg at home but did not use ice or heat. He took Tylenol for pain without significant relief. He reports a limp when walking and some difficulty with weight bearing, though able to bear weight. Pain is localized to the lateral aspect of the right knee.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient goes to the trampoline park infrequently, and this was his first visit. The activity was for recreational purposes. Patient does not have a consistent or regular exercise regimen. Patient reports reluctance about seeking medical care. Patient is married. Regarding diet, patient is not tracking calories or macros and is not following a specific diet plan. Patient is attempting to watch carbohydrate intake but not counting them. Patient denies being on a keto diet. Patient checks blood glucose levels approximately 4-5 times per week when he remembers. Patient was previously advised to obtain a blood pressure cuff for home monitoring but has not done so.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 180/80 mmHg
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated
Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally
Right Knee: Tenderness on lateral aspect; no tenderness on medial aspect. Able to bend and straighten knee with pain on some movements. Limp noted on gait. Ecchymosis and edema on lateral aspect. No joint effusion appreciated. Decent overall range of motion.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - Lateral ligament strain
   - Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling
   - Referred to physical therapy to strengthen muscles around the area and prevent further injury
   - Further imaging may be considered if pain persists
   - Advised that this is a common injury that tends to heal on its own

2. Hypertension
   - Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily
   - Ordered echocardiogram
   - Discussed that blood pressure control may need medication modification

3. Diabetes
   - Ordered A1C to assess long-term glycemic control
   - Ordered lipid panel; medication adjustments may be made if needed
   - Advised to increase frequency of home blood glucose monitoring to 2-3 times daily
